salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: In Psalm 13:1, the psalmist asks how long the Lord will hide his face from him.
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: The question about the hidden face is part of the psalmist's lament.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Psalm 13:1 and see the second question.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: In Psalm 13:1, tap what the psalmist feels God is hiding.
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: He feels God's face is hidden, an image of no visible answer.

feedbackWrong.a: That speaks of how long he fears it will last, not what is hidden.
feedbackWrong.c: That says from whom the face is hidden, not what is hidden.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: Look for what belongs to God in the sentence.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: According to Psalm 13:2, what does the psalmist feel in his heart day after day?
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: The lament names the daily sorrow without hiding the pain.

feedbackWrong.b: The text speaks of sorrow, not of pride in the heart.
feedbackWrong.c: Joy is asked for in other Psalms; here the feeling is different.
feedbackWrong.d: The problem is the felt delay, but the feeling named is sorrow.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: Read the feeling named in the middle of the verse.

options.c: Joy

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: Put Psalm 13:1 in the order of the text.
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: The questions pile up: feared forgetting and a hidden face.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the short question; the hidden face closes the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: The verse begins with the shortest question.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: In Psalm 13:3, what does the psalmist ask God to light up in him?
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: He asks for lit-up eyes, an image of life and help from God.

feedbackWrong.a: Paths are not mentioned in this request in Psalm 13:3.
feedbackWrong.c: The enemies appear in the next verse, not in this request.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: See the request made to God.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: What does Psalm 13:5 convey that connects to this context?
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: After asking and pleading, he states his trust in God's grace.

feedbackWrong.b: The enemy is exactly the one he asks not to win.
feedbackWrong.c: He does not give up: he keeps talking to God until he trusts.

options.c: Giving up on prayer

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: In Psalm 13:1–3, after the questions the psalmist gives up asking God for help.
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: He does not give up: from the questions he moves to asking God to look at him.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Psalm 13:3: he asks God to look at him.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: See what he does in the third verse.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: In Psalm 13:5, tap the word that marks the turn toward trust.
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: This word opens the turn: after the pain, he states his trust.

feedbackWrong.b: This word speaks of rescue, but the turn begins earlier.
feedbackWrong.c: This word speaks of who will rejoice; it does not mark the turn.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: Look for the first word of the verse.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: How does Psalm 13:3 relate to the questions in Psalm 13:1–2?
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: The questions become a request: he calls on God to look at him.

feedbackWrong.a: The text tells of no answer received; he is still asking.
feedbackWrong.c: The prayer continues in the following verses on the same theme.
feedbackWrong.d: He keeps talking to God; he does not leave the conversation.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: See the move from questions to request.

options.a: He thanks God for an answer already received
options.b: He turns his pain into a request addressed to God
options.c: He ends the prayer and changes the subject
options.d: He accuses God and leaves the conversation

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: How does the prayer move forward in Psalm 13:1–3?
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: From question to laying out the pain, the prayer reaches a direct request.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the questions; the request to God comes in the third verse.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: The direct request is the end point.

options.b: He lays out sorrow and enemy
options.c: He asks God to look at him

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: In Psalm 13:3, what sleep does the psalmist ask not to fall into?
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: The request for light is tied to staying alive before God.

feedbackWrong.b: Night is not mentioned in this request; the danger named is another.
feedbackWrong.c: He is not asking for rest here, but for rescue from death.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: See the danger named at the end of the verse.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: What connects Psalm 13:5 to Psalm 42:11?
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: In both Psalms, the sad soul is called to hope in God.

feedbackWrong.a: Both Psalms lay the pain before God; they do not hide it from him.
feedbackWrong.c: In the Psalms the enemy is the problem, never the ground of trust.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: Compare the final attitude of the two Psalms.

options.c: Trusting only in the enemy

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: Psalm 13:1–5 shows that one can lament before God and still trust in his grace.
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: The same Psalm holds the honest questions and the final trust.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of the Psalm: after the lament, he trusts in grace.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: Compare the beginning and the end of the Psalm.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: In Psalm 13:5, tap what the psalmist declares he trusts in.
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: His trust rests on God's grace, even without seeing the answer.

feedbackWrong.b: The heart is what will rejoice; the trust rests on something else.
feedbackWrong.c: Salvation is the reason for joy; the trust is placed in grace.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: See the verb trust and what comes after it.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: What reading does Psalm 13:1–5 support about lamenting before God?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: The whole Psalm shows honest questions arriving at trust in grace.

feedbackWrong.a: The one who asks here ends up trusting, not without faith.
feedbackWrong.c: Trust appears without denying the sorrow mentioned before.
feedbackWrong.d: The pain is laid before God in clear words, not hidden.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: See the whole path of the Psalm.

options.a: Asking God questions is always a lack of faith
options.b: Honest lament can move toward trust
options.c: Trusting requires pretending there is no suffering
options.d: Pain should be hidden in prayer

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: Which sequence reveals the logic of the prayer in Psalm 13?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: Question, request and trust form the path of this prayer of lament.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the Psalm: questions, request and final trust.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: Trust is the last step of the Psalm.

options.c: He trusts in God's grace

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: In Psalm 13:5, the psalmist's heart will rejoice in God's what?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: The hoped-for joy is in the salvation that comes from God.

feedbackWrong.a: Grace is where he trusts; the joy is tied to another word.
feedbackWrong.c: Justice is not mentioned in this final verse.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: See the reason for joy at the end.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.question: What connects Psalm 13:5 to Habakkuk 3:18?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, joy in God appears in the middle of lack and pain.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts speak to God and about him; they are not silent before him.
feedbackWrong.b: In both cases there is present suffering, and still joy in God.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-.hint: Compare the joy mentioned in the two texts.

options.c: Joy in God despite the losses

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: In Psalm 51:10, the psalmist asks for a pure heart without asking for inner renewal.
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: He asks for both: a pure heart and a renewed spirit within him.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the second part of Psalm 51:10 about the spirit.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: Look at the second part of the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: In Psalm 51:7, tap what the psalmist asks to be purified with.
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: The image of purification asked of God uses hyssop.

feedbackWrong.b: Snow compares the result of being washed, not the means named earlier.
feedbackWrong.c: Clean is the expected result, not what he asks to be purified with.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: Look for the means named at the start.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: According to Psalm 51:11, what does the psalmist ask God not to take from him?
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: He asks not to lose the presence of God's Holy Spirit.

feedbackWrong.b: His sins he asks to be blotted out, not kept.
feedbackWrong.c: His joy he asks to have back in the next verse.
feedbackWrong.d: The people are not mentioned in this request in Psalm 51:11.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: Read the second part of the verse.

options.c: His joy

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: Put Psalm 51:10 in the order of the text.
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: First the pure heart created, then the spirit renewed within.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the pure heart; the steadfast spirit closes the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: The verse begins with the heart.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: In Psalm 51:7, whiter than what will the psalmist become when washed?
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: The comparison shows complete cleansing: whiter than snow.

feedbackWrong.a: Stone does not appear in this comparison of cleansing.
feedbackWrong.c: Water is not the comparison used at the end of the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: See the comparison at the end of the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: What does Psalm 51:10 convey that connects to this context?
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: The context sums up the request: a heart created by God himself.

feedbackWrong.a: The request includes change within, not just declared forgiveness.
feedbackWrong.b: The one who creates the heart is God, to whom the request is made.

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: See to whom the request is made.

options.a: Forgiveness with no change at all
options.c: A heart created by God

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: In Psalm 51:12–13, the psalmist will teach others before asking for the joy of salvation.
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: First he asks for joy back; teaching comes as the next step.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the order: the "Então" of 51:13 comes after the request in 51:12.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: Notice the word that opens verse 13.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: In Psalm 51:13, tap the word that marks the step after renewal.
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: This word links the renewal received to the teaching that will follow.

feedbackWrong.a: These are the ones who will be taught, not the mark of the next step.
feedbackWrong.c: These are the ones who will turn, at the end of the verse.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: Look for the first word of the verse.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: How does Psalm 51:13 relate to the request in Psalm 51:12?
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: Teaching appears as the next fruit of the joy and renewal asked for.

feedbackWrong.a: He will teach God's ways; the turning is to him.
feedbackWrong.b: The "Então" shows teaching after the request for restoration.
feedbackWrong.c: The joy asked for leads to teaching; it does not replace it.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: See the order between the two verses.

options.a: Others turn without any relation to God
options.b: He will teach others before being restored
options.c: Restored joy makes teaching anyone unnecessary
options.d: Once restored, he starts teaching others

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: How does the request move forward in Psalm 51:7–12?
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: From cleansing to a new heart, the request reaches restored joy.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with cleansing; restored joy is the last request.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: Joy returned is the end point.

options.a: He asks to be cleansed of sins

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: In Psalm 51:12, what does the psalmist ask God to restore to him?
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: He asks for the joy tied to God's salvation back.

feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of regained innocence in this verse.
feedbackWrong.c: Presence is the request of the previous verse, with another word.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: See what he wants to receive back.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: What connects Psalm 51:10 to Ezekiel 36:26?
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: The Psalm's request and Ezekiel's promise speak of a heart given by God.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts tie forgiveness to a transformed heart.
feedbackWrong.c: In both texts, the one who gives the new heart is God.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: Compare who acts on the heart.

options.c: A heart made by man

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: Psalm 51:9–10 shows that the forgiveness asked for includes cleansing of sins and a heart created by God.
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: The request joins blotting out iniquities and creating a pure heart.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the two requests side by side in Psalm 51:9–10.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: Compare the requests of the two verses.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: In Psalm 51:10, tap the phrase that shows the action asked of God.
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: The request places God as the one who creates the new heart in him.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the renewed spirit, in the second part of the request.
feedbackWrong.c: That is what will be created, not the action asked of God.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: Look for the verb addressed to God.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: What reading does Psalm 51:10 support about the renewal of the heart?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: The request is made to God because he creates and renews within.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of heart and spirit within, not of appearance.

feedbackWrong.d: The verb is a request to God, not the psalmist's own work.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: See to whom the request is addressed.

options.a: Renewal is only an outward appearance
options.b: A steadfast spirit comes from human effort alone
options.c: God is the one who creates the pure heart in him

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: Which sequence reveals the path of renewal in the Bible?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: From the Psalm's request to Ezekiel's promise, God renews within.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the Bible: request in Psalms and promise in Ezekiel.

options.a: The psalmist asks for a pure heart
options.b: God promises to give a new heart

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: In Psalm 51:10, what should the heart created by God be like?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.feedbackCorrect: The word sums up the renewal asked for: a clean heart before God.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.hint: See the adjective tied to the heart.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mi.question: What connects Psalm 51:9 to Psalm 32:1?

options.b: Forgiveness with no joy at all

salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.question: According to Psalm 51:11, what does the psalmist ask God not to take from him?
salmos-sem-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: He asks not to lose the presence of God's Holy Spirit.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: This word opens the turn: after the pain, he states his trust.

feedbackWrong.b: This word names what trust rests on; it does not mark the turn.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.hint: Look for the first word of the verse.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.question: How do the requests link together in Psalm 51:7–10?
salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: From purification to forgiveness, the request reaches a heart created by God.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with purification; the created heart is the last request.

salmos-cam-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.hint: The created heart closes the sequence.

options.c: Request for a created heart

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.question: Psalms 13 and 51 show that prayer includes lamenting the delay and asking for a renewed heart.
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: One Psalm laments before God; the other asks for a heart he creates.

feedbackWrong.false: Compare the lament of Psalm 13 with the request in Psalm 51:10.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.hint: Compare the two prayers in the challenge.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.question: In Psalm 51:10, tap the phrase that shows the action asked of God.
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: The request places God as the one who creates the new heart in him.

feedbackWrong.a: That says where renewal happens, in the second part.
feedbackWrong.b: That is what will be created, not the action asked of God.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.hint: Look for the verb addressed to God.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.question: What joint reading do Psalms 13 and 51 support about prayer?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: One Psalm brings pain to God; the other brings guilt and asks for a new heart.

feedbackWrong.a: Psalm 13 trusts without denying the sorrow mentioned before.
feedbackWrong.b: Both Psalms lay pain and guilt before God in clear words.
feedbackWrong.d: Psalm 51 asks God to create the heart, not effort alone.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.hint: Put together the theme of the two prayers.

options.b: Praying is hiding pain and guilt from God
options.c: God hears lament and renews the heart
options.d: Renewal depends only on human effort

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.question: Which sequence reveals the path of prayer in these Psalms?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: From trusting lament to God's promise, the path reaches teaching others.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the path: lament, God's promise and teaching others.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.hint: Start with the lament that trusts.

options.a: The psalmist laments and trusts in grace
options.b: God promises a new heart and Spirit
options.c: The renewed one teaches others to return

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.question: In Psalm 13:5, in what of God does the psalmist declare he trusts?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: Even in lament, his trust rests on God's grace.

feedbackWrong.a: Salvation is the reason for the joy named after the trust.
feedbackWrong.c: Justice is not mentioned in this final verse of the Psalm.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.hint: See what is named after trust.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.question: What connects Psalm 13:5 to Habakkuk 3:18?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, joy in God appears in the middle of lack and pain.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts speak to God and about him; they are not silent before him.
feedbackWrong.b: In both cases there is present suffering, and still joy in God.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.hint: Compare the joy mentioned in the two texts.

options.c: Joy in God despite the losses

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.question: In Psalm 51:11, tap whom the psalmist asks God not to take from him.
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: He asks not to lose the Holy Spirit, God's presence with him.

feedbackWrong.a: That is part of the request, but it does not name whom he fears losing.
feedbackWrong.c: From the presence he asks not to be cast away; taking is said of the Spirit.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.hint: See the object of the verb take.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.question: Which sequence reveals the fruit of renewal in Psalm 51?
salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.feedbackCorrect: From a heart created to joy returned, the fruit is others coming back to God.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the Psalm: heart, joy and others coming back to God.

salmos-pro-salmos-lamento-03-desafio-ora.hint: Others coming back to God is the last fruit.

options.a: The heart is created pure by God
options.b: The joy of salvation is restored
options.c: He sees sinners coming back to God

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: In Psalm 1:2, the blessed one meditates on the law of the Lord day and night.
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: The text ties delight in the law to thinking on it day and night.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Psalm 1:2 and see the habit described at the end of the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: In Psalm 1:1, tap the group whose counsel the man does not follow.
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: The first group named is the wicked, whose counsel he refuses.

feedbackWrong.a: Sinners appear on the path where he does not stand.
feedbackWrong.b: Mockers appear in the circle where he does not sit.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: Look for the first group named.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: According to Psalm 1:1, where does the blessed one not sit?
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: The text says he does not sit in the circle of mockers.

feedbackWrong.b: The still waters are in Psalm 23:2, not in this verse.
feedbackWrong.c: The house of the Lord appears in Psalm 23:6.
feedbackWrong.d: The green pastures are in Psalm 23:2.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: Read the last part of the verse.

options.c: In the house of the Lord

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: Put Psalm 1:1 in the order of the text.
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: The order is walk, stand and sit, ever more settled on the wrong path.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the counsel of the wicked; the circle of mockers closes the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: The verse begins by calling the man blessed.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: In Psalm 1:2, what does the blessed one have in the law of the Lord?
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: The law of the Lord is no burden to him: it is where his delight is.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of joy in the law, not fear of it.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of doubt, but of delight in the law.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: See the feeling tied to the law.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: What does Psalm 1:2 convey that connects to this context?
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: The context sums up the verse: joy in the law and constant thought on it.

feedbackWrong.b: The counsel of the wicked is what he avoids, in Psalm 1:1.
feedbackWrong.c: He does not run from reading; he meditates on the law always.

options.c: Running from all reading

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: In Psalm 1:1–2, the text contrasts the company avoided with delight in the law of the Lord.
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: The word "Antes" turns the contrast: he avoids some and delights in the law.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the move from Psalm 1:1 to 1:2 and notice the contrast.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: Notice the word that opens the second verse.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: In Psalm 1:2, tap the word that marks the contrast with the previous verse.
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: This word opens the contrast with the company refused before.

feedbackWrong.a: This word marks time, not the contrast between the verses.
feedbackWrong.c: This word says where his heart is; it does not mark the turn.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: Look for the first word of the verse.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: How does Psalm 1:2 relate to Psalm 1:1?
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: Against the bad counsel refused, the text sets delight in the law of the Lord.

feedbackWrong.b: Thinking on the law continually is a path of obedience, not a substitute.
feedbackWrong.c: The reflection is day and night, not only at one time.
feedbackWrong.d: He refuses the counsel of the wicked; he does not accept just any direction.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: Think of the contrast between the two verses.

options.a: It shows where he seeks direction instead of bad counsel
options.b: It explains that reflecting replaces obeying the law
options.c: It states that the law is only for the night
options.d: It shows that he accepts any counsel he receives

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: How does the scene move forward in Psalm 1:1–2?
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: First the refusal, then delight in the law, and then the constant habit.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what he avoids; the habit at all times closes the scene.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: The constant habit is the end point.

options.c: Meditation at all times

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: In Psalm 1:2, what does he do in the law day and night?
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: He does not just read: he thinks on the law continually.

feedbackWrong.a: The text shows constant attention to the law, not neglect of it.
feedbackWrong.c: The habit described is the opposite of forgetting the law.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: See the repeated action at the end of the verse.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: What connects Psalm 1:2 to Joshua 1:8?
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, God's word fills the thoughts day and night.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts bring the reader closer to the law, not away from it.
feedbackWrong.b: Listening to mockers is what Psalm 1:1 says to avoid.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: Compare the habit named in the two texts.

options.c: Meditating day and night

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: Psalm 1:1–2 presents happiness as the fruit of following the counsel of the wicked in moderation.
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: The text does not bargain with that counsel: happiness is in the law of the Lord.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Psalm 1:1: he does not walk in the counsel of the wicked.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: See what the first verse denies.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: In Psalm 23:4, tap the phrase that shows the Lord's presence in the valley.
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: The Lord's presence with him is the center of trust in the valley.

feedbackWrong.b: That describes the hard setting, not the Lord's presence.
feedbackWrong.c: That says what he does not fear; the presence comes in the reason after.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: Look for the phrase about companionship.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: What reading does Psalm 1:1–2 support about happiness?
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: Happiness is tied to refusing bad counsel and loving God's law.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says not to walk in the counsel of the wicked.
feedbackWrong.c: It is precisely in the law of the Lord that his delight is.
feedbackWrong.d: The blessed one has a clear direction: the law of the Lord.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: Compare each option with the two verses.

options.a: Happiness comes from heeding all counsel equally
options.b: Happiness is living guided by God's word
options.c: Happiness depends on avoiding the law of the Lord
options.d: Happiness needs no direction for life

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: Which sequence reveals the path of the blessed one in the Bible?
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: From refusal to a habit in the law, the path reaches happy trust in God.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the text: refusal, habit in the law and trust in God.

options.b: He always thinks on God's law
options.c: Whoever trusts in the Lord is happy

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: In Psalm 1:1, what does the text call the man who avoids bad counsel?
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: This is the name the Psalm gives to one who lives on God's path.

feedbackWrong.a: A mocker is whom he avoids in the circle, not who he is.
feedbackWrong.c: The wicked is whom he does not listen to, not who he is.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: See the first word of the Psalm.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.question: What connects Psalm 1:1 to Jeremiah 17:7?
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.feedbackCorrect: Both texts call happy the one who lives turned toward God.

feedbackWrong.b: The text refuses bad company, not all company.
feedbackWrong.c: Psalm 1:1 refuses bad counsel; it takes no delight in it.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventura.hint: Compare what the two texts call this man.

options.c: Delight in bad counsel

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: In Psalm 23:4, the psalmist states that he will never go through any dark valley.
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: The Psalm speaks of walking through the valley, but with the Lord present in it.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the start of Psalm 23:4: he considers walking through the valley.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: Look at the start of the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: In Psalm 23:1, tap the title the psalmist gives the Lord.
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: The psalmist calls the Lord his shepherd right at the opening.

feedbackWrong.a: That word speaks of what he will not lack, not the Lord's title.
feedbackWrong.c: That word speaks of provision, not of who the Lord is.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: Look for what he calls the Lord.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: According to Psalm 23:2, beside what does the Lord lead the psalmist?
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: After the pastures, the text speaks of the still waters.

feedbackWrong.b: The valley appears in Psalm 23:4, at another point in the Psalm.
feedbackWrong.c: That image is from Psalm 1:1, not this verse.
feedbackWrong.d: That expression is from Psalm 13:3, not this Psalm.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: Read the second part of the verse.

options.c: The circle of mockers

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: Put Psalm 23:3 in the order of the text.
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: First the soul is refreshed, then comes the guiding and its reason.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the refreshed soul; the reason for the guiding closes the verse.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: The verse begins with the soul.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: In Psalm 23:2, beside waters of what is the psalmist led?
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: The waters are of rest: the shepherd leads to a place of repose.

feedbackWrong.a: Righteousness appears in the paths of Psalm 23:3, not in the waters.
feedbackWrong.c: Death appears in the valley of Psalm 23:4, not in the waters.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: See the name given to the waters.

salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: What does Psalm 23:1 convey that connects to this context?
salmos-sem-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: If the Lord is the shepherd, care and provision come from him.

feedbackWrong.a: The shepherd guides; the path is not walked without direction.
feedbackWrong.c: The verse states precisely that there is a shepherd present.

options.c: Sheep without a shepherd

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: In Psalm 23:4, the psalmist does not fear in the valley because the Lord is with him.
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: The reason for not fearing is the Lord's presence with him in the valley.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Psalm 23:4 and see the reason given after "não temerei".

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: Look for the reason after the statement.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: In Psalm 23:4, tap the word that introduces the reason for not fearing.
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: This word links not fearing to the Lord's presence with him.

feedbackWrong.a: This word speaks of company, but does not introduce the reason.
feedbackWrong.b: This word opens the case of the valley, not the reason for not fearing.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: Look for the link between not fearing and having company.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: How does Psalm 23:3 explain the Lord's guiding in paths of righteousness?
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: The shepherd's guiding is tied to God's own name and character.

feedbackWrong.b: The text ties the guiding precisely to God's name.
feedbackWrong.c: The reason named is God's name, not the psalmist's strength.
feedbackWrong.d: In the next verse, the guiding goes on even into the valley.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: See the reason named at the end of the verse.

options.a: He guides for his own name's sake
options.b: He guides with no regard for his character
options.c: He guides to prove the psalmist's strength
options.d: He guides only when there is no danger

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: How does the care move forward in Psalm 23:3–4?
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: From the restored soul to guiding, the care reaches presence in the valley.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the restored soul; presence in the valley is the last step.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: The valley is the end point.

options.b: He guides in paths of righteousness
options.c: He stays present in the dark valley

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: In Psalm 23:3, in paths of what does the Lord guide the psalmist?
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: The shepherd does not guide along just any path, but along right paths.

feedbackWrong.a: Shadow describes the valley of Psalm 23:4, not the paths.
feedbackWrong.c: Rest describes the waters of Psalm 23:2, not the paths.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: See the name of the paths.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: What connects Psalm 23:1 to Ezekiel 34:15?
salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, God himself shepherds his people.

feedbackWrong.a: The shepherd in both texts is God himself, not human leaders.
feedbackWrong.c: Both texts affirm God's care, not abandonment.

salmos-cam-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: See who shepherds in both texts.

options.c: Sheep with no care at all

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: In Psalm 23:1, lacking nothing means the psalmist will have all his wishes fulfilled.
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: The text ties not lacking to the shepherd's care, not to fulfilled wishes.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread who provides in the verse: it is the Lord as shepherd.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: See who the subject of the verse is.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: In Psalm 23:4, tap the phrase that upholds trust in the valley.
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: Trust rests on the Lord's presence, not on the absence of the valley.

feedbackWrong.a: That says what he does not fear; the support comes from God's presence.
feedbackWrong.c: That describes the hard place, not the support of trust.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: Look for the phrase about company.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: What reading does Psalm 23:4 support about fear in suffering?
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: Comfort comes from God present with rod and staff inside the valley.

feedbackWrong.b: In the text, rod and staff comfort; they do not reject.
feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of walking through the valley, not being spared from it.
feedbackWrong.d: The text states the opposite: "tu estás comigo".

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: See what brings comfort inside the valley.

options.a: God's presence upholds trust in the valley
options.b: Rod and staff are signs of divine rejection
options.c: God removes every valley before it comes
options.d: The valley proves God abandoned the psalmist

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: Which sequence reveals the shepherd thread in the Bible's story?
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: From the Psalm to Ezekiel and to Jesus, God reveals himself as his people's shepherd.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the Bible: Psalms, Ezekiel and then the Gospel of John.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: Follow the order: Psalms, prophet and Gospel.

options.a: The Lord is the psalmist's shepherd
options.b: God promises to shepherd his people
options.c: Jesus presents himself as the good shepherd

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: In Psalm 23:6, what will follow the psalmist along with goodness?
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: Goodness and mercy go with the one who trusts, every day.

feedbackWrong.b: Enemies appear at the banquet of Psalm 23:5, not following the psalmist.
feedbackWrong.c: Shadow belongs to the valley of Psalm 23:4, not the final company.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: See the pair that goes with the psalmist.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.question: What connects Psalm 23:1 to John 10:11?
salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.feedbackCorrect: Jesus presents himself with the same image: the good shepherd of God's people.

feedbackWrong.b: In both texts the sheep have a shepherd who guides them.
feedbackWrong.c: In both texts the shepherd cares; neither speaks of abandonment.

salmos-pro-salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o.hint: See how Jesus presents himself in John.

options.c: A shepherd who abandons
